items.title: Navigating the transition shock: a study on the professional socialization of nursing students based on Douyin content—A comparison of manual thematic analysis and analysis assisted by large language models
items.abstract: Clinical internships are a critical stage in the professional socialisation of nursing students, but negative experiences during these internships may lead to a decline in professional identity or even the loss of talent. The Douyin (the Chinese version of TikTok) platform features many internship narratives spontaneously shared by nursing interns, providing a unique data source for understanding their narrative expressions; however, systematic qualitative research on this topic remains lacking. This study explores the thematic characteristics of professional socialisation among nursing interns on the Douyin platform and compares manual thematic analysis with analysis using the DeepSeek R1 large language model in theme identification. Using a human-machine parallel qualitative research design, we collected 40 short videos posted by nursing interns and 431 valid comments from Douyin. We conducted manual thematic analysis (using NVivo 12) and an independent analysis using the DeepSeek R1 large language model. Using Duchscher’s three-stage model of transitional shock as the theoretical framework, we systematically compared the thematic identification results of the two methods. The integrated thematic matrix shows that nursing interns’ narratives revolve around three themes tied to the stages of their clinical practice: the early stage is marked by value conflicts; the middle stage by superficial role identification; and the late stage by a tendency toward either professional self-integration or professional disengagement. This study tentatively summarises the above phenomena as “structural value disconnection,” “the tension between superficial adaptation and deep internalisation,” and “value-integration outcomes” versus “value-disengagement outcomes.” These concepts are inductive descriptions based on cross-sectional data and require further validation through longitudinal research. The three stages correspond to the “Doing-Being-Knowing” framework in Duchscher’s theory of transitional shock and involve three aspects of professional socialisation: acquiring knowledge and skills, internalising values and norms, and forming role identity. Under the specific input conditions of this study (manual exposure to multimodal information, with DeepSeek R1 receiving only text), the two methods showed strong consistency in identifying core themes. At the same time, each captured complementary themes that the other missed. Nursing interns’ narratives reflect thematic patterns tied to the internship phase, showing a progression from value conflicts and superficial adaptation to internalisation or withdrawal. The complementary nature of manual analysis and large language model analysis provides a methodological framework for qualitative research in nursing. The findings suggest that educators should integrate value guidance throughout the entire clinical practicum process and, through measures such as pre-practicum psychological preparation, improvement of the mentor-student relationship, and comprehensive psychological support mechanisms, facilitate students’ transition from behavioural compliance to value alignment.

items.title: Next-Generation Therapeutics: Synergizing QSAR, Nanotechnology, and Green Chemistry for Advanced Drug Development
items.abstract: Introduction: Traditional pharmaceutical development faces critical challenges: drug development costs exceed $2.6 billion per approved drug, timelines extend 10-15 years, and 40% of new chemical entities demonstrate inadequate bioavailability. Conventional approaches rely on empirical screening generating 50-100 kg waste per kilogram of active pharmaceutical ingredient. The pharmaceutical industry urgently requires transformative innovation integrating computational intelligence, advanced delivery systems, and sustainable manufacturing. Methods: This comprehensive review integrates three complementary technological paradigms: (1) QSAR-powered artificial intelligence employing machine learning algorithms for computational drug discovery, reducing chemical synthesis requirements by 85-90%; (2) Nanotechnology-enabled delivery systems (liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, cubosomes, transethosomes) overcoming biological barriers and enhancing bioavailability 10-100 fold; and (3) Green chemistry principles enabling sustainable synthesis through catalytic reactions, biocatalysis, and continuous manufacturing, reducing waste generation by 60-90%. Results: Integrated QSAR-nano-green chemistry approaches demonstrate remarkable benefits compared to conventional methods: 92% waste reduction (95 kg → 8 kg per kilogram product), 82% energy reduction (250 → 45 kWh/kg), 47% cost reduction ($650 → $343/kg), and 92% timeline acceleration (48 → 4 hours). QSAR screening reduces experimental compounds from 200-300 to 15-20, while nanoformulations enhance bioavailability and targeting efficiency. Green chemistry manufacturing achieves pharmaceutical-grade quality with minimal environmental burden. Conclusion: Synergistic convergence of QSAR, nanotechnology, and green chemistry represents paradigm shift in pharmaceutical innovation. This integrated approach enables development of therapeutics that are more effective, safer, more sustainable, and economically accessible globally democratizing drug development across academic, industry, and developing country sectors.

items.title: Operational Epistemic Situational Awareness in Agentic Orchestration
items.abstract: Long-running agent workflows can lose task scope, source custody, authority, current environment state, unresolved conflicts, or knowledge of what another worker is doing. Operational Epistemic Situational Awareness (ESA) is proposed as the capability to maintain and query an evidence-qualified model of those conditions and to govern continuation when that model becomes stale, conflicted, missing, or outside authority. The architecture uses a governed meaning substrate as an orchestration sidecar, but a sidecar is not awareness by itself. Agent check-ins can be false or stale; receipts can record claims without proving effects; exclusive task claims can deadlock; handoffs can be unaccepted; and unmediated tools can bypass the substrate. The system must distinguish asserted, observed, inferred, stale, conflicted, and unknown state; combine voluntary reports with independent observations; preserve liveness and recovery; and govern sensitive operational data. This paper defines an operational state model, check-in and claim leases, accepted handoff capsules, evidence postures, refusal and escalation outcomes, bypass and availability conditions, cold-boot orientation through the Governed Meaning Base, realization funnel, and comparative evaluation. It makes no claim of consciousness or privileged agent self-knowledge.

items.title: Outcomes of informal and formal care models at the end of life: An AI-supported systematic review
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Multimorbidity and functional decline become increasingly prevalent with age, particularly in those near the end of life. This poses critical challenges for both families and society in providing adequate care. However, it remains unclear which type of care yields better outcomes. AIM: To systematically assess the impact of informal care, formal care, and a combination of both on health outcomes, healthcare utilization, and costs of care for older adults near the end of life. DESIGN: A systematic review with narrative synthesis was registered on PROSPERO (CRD42024512003). Screening was assisted by machine learning tool ASReview, and study quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool, with support from large language model TXYZ.AI. DATA SOURCES: Articles published between database inception and June 4th, 2025 were identified in PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL. RESULTS: Thirty-six studies, including 20 observational and 16 interventional were included. Most observational studies examined place of death, with some associations involving informal care pointing towards lower home death or greater hospital death. In contrast, physician and nurse home visits were associated with a greater likelihood of home death. Specialized formal care interventions generally reported improvements in quality of life and reductions in healthcare use. Quality assessment showed 85.2% AI-human agreement, with 44.4% of studies meeting all seven quality criteria. DISCUSSION: Informal care did not necessarily facilitate home death, whereas formal home-based care was linked to a greater likelihood of home death. Interventional evidence also suggests broader benefits of specialized formal care, although certainty was limited by methodological concerns.

items.title: Pemanfaatan Artificial Intelligence Dalam Deteksi Dini, Early Warning System, dan Sistem Rujukan Kegawatdaruratan Pada Resource-Limited Settings: A Narrative Review
items.abstract: Background: Healthcare facilities with limited resources face various challenges in early detection and emergency referral systems, including shortages of healthcare personnel, inadequate infrastructure, and the limited accuracy of conventional screening methods. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has the potential to serve as a solution to improve the quality of clinical decision-making under these conditions. Objective: This scientific paper aims to identify and synthesize current evidence regarding the use of AI in early detection, early warning systems, and triage. Methods: This study is a narrative review using the PubMed and Google Scholar databases. English-language articles published between 2019 and 2026 that discussed the implementation of AI in early detection or emergency referral systems in resource-limited settings were included. Of the 2,376 articles identified, 16 met the inclusion criteria. Results: The articles were predominantly focused on early detection and early warning systems (50%), followed by triage and referral systems (31%), and health system strengthening (19%). Machine Learning and Deep Learning were the most commonly used AI methods. Several studies demonstrated high performance, with AUC values ranging from 0.80 to 0.97. AI was shown to improve the accuracy of sepsis detection, patient prioritization, and support faster and more objective referral decision-making. Conclusion: AI has the potential to enhance early detection, triage, and emergency referral systems in healthcare facilities with limited resources, although its implementation continues to face challenges related to infrastructure, user trust, as well as regulatory and data governance aspects.

items.title: PEMANFAATAN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DALAM PENGINJILAN DIGITAL BAGIGENERASI Z MELALUI MEDIA SOSIAL:KAJIAN TEOLOGIS
items.abstract: Abstrak Tujuan penelitian ini adalah untuk mengkaji pemanfaatan Artificial Intelligence (AI) secara teologis sebagai sarana pendukung penginjilan digital bagi Generasi Z melalui media sosial. Perkembangan AI dan media sosial telah mengubah cara Generasi Z berkomunikasi, memperoleh informasi, membangun relasi, dan berinteraksi dengan pesan-pesan keagamaan. Perubahan tersebut memberikan peluang baru bagi gereja untuk memberitakan Injil melalui berbagai platform digital, sekaligus menghadirkan tantangan teologis dan etis berkaitan dengan autentisitas, tanggung jawab manusia, otoritas Kitab Suci, pengaruh algoritma, dan dimensi relasional dalam penginjilan. Penelitian ini menggunakan metode kualitatif deskriptif melalui studi kepustakaan terhadap berbagai kajian teologis, misiologis, dan interdisipliner mengenai AI, teologi digital, media sosial, Generasi Z, dan penginjilan Kristen. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa AI dapat mendukung penginjilan digital melalui produksi konten, penerjemahan, personalisasi pesan, pengembangan visual, dan perluasan jangkauan pemberitaan Injil. Namun, AI tidak dapat menggantikan manusia sebagai saksi Kristus karena tidak memiliki iman, pengalaman spiritual, tanggung jawab moral, dan kehadiran relasional sebagaimana manusia. Oleh karena itu, AI perlu ditempatkan sebagai sarana misi, bukan subjek misi. Kristus tetap menjadi pusat Injil, Kitab Suci menjadi dasar pemberitaan, manusia menjadi saksi, AI berfungsi sebagai sarana pendukung, media sosial menjadi ruang komunikasi dan perjumpaan, sedangkan arah akhir penginjilan digital adalah terbentuknya relasi dan pemuridan. Kata-kata kunci: Artificial Intelligence, penginjilan digital, Generasi Z, media sosial, teologi digital, pemuridan abstract The purpose of this study is to examine the theological use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) as a supporting medium for digital evangelism among Generation Z through social media. The rapid development of AI and social media has transformed the way Generation Z communicates, obtains information, builds relationships, and encounters religious messages. This transformation provides new opportunities for the church to proclaim the gospel through digital platforms, while also raising theological and ethical challenges concerning authenticity, human responsibility, biblical authority, algorithmic influence, and the relational nature of evangelism. This study employs a descriptive qualitative method through a literature review of theological, missiological, and interdisciplinary studies concerning AI, digital theology, social media, Generation Z, and Christian evangelism. The findings indicate that AI can support digital evangelism through content production, translation, personalization, visual development, and wider dissemination of gospel messages. However, AI cannot replace human beings as witnesses of Christ because it does not possess faith, spiritual experience, moral responsibility, or relational presence. Therefore, AI should be positioned as a means of mission rather than a subject of mission. Christ remains the center of the gospel, Scripture remains the foundation of its message, human beings remain witnesses, AI functions as a supporting tool, social media becomes a space for communication and encounter, and the ultimate direction of digital evangelism is relationship and discipleship. Key words: Artificial Intelligence, digital evangelism, Z Generation, social media, digital theology, discipleship

items.title: PEMANFAATAN KECERDASAN BUATAN DALAM PEMBELAJARAN BAHASA ARAB: ANALISIS PENGGUNAAN CHATGPT UNTUK PENGEMBANGAN KETERAMPILAN MENULIS MAHASISWA
items.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (Generative AI), such as ChatGPT, has brought significant changes to higher education, including Arabic language learning for non-native speakers (Arabic as a Foreign Language). Writing skills (Maharah al-Kitabah) are considered a relatively complex productive skill. Learners are required not only to master word formation (Sarf) and Arabic grammar (Nahwu), but also to organize ideas coherently and logically. This article employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach based on the PRISMA 2020 standards to map the use of ChatGPT in Arabic writing, examine the reliability of AI in Arabic grammar, and identify research gaps that remain underexplored. The review findings indicate that ChatGPT can serve as a useful writing partner (human-AI co-writer), particularly for generating ideas, enriching vocabulary, and correcting basic grammatical errors. However, AI still frequently produces errors or “hallucinations” when dealing with morphologically complex words, variations in Arabic dialects, and unvocalized texts. As a result, AI-generated writing may appear linguistically polished on the surface while containing grammatical inaccuracies. Furthermore, excessive reliance on AI may pose risks to academic integrity, while AI detection tools themselves often produce inaccurate results when identifying Arabic-language texts (false positives). This review also finds that existing research remains overly focused on English, tends to examine only the final writing outcomes without investigating students’ cognitive processes, and has paid limited attention to AI models specifically developed for the Arab region, such as ALLaM and Jais. Therefore, the approach to AI-assisted learning needs to shift from merely using AI toward purposeful and reflective utilization through frameworks such as the Spiral Learning Model and Genre-Based Pedagogy, so that AI functions as a scaffold without diminishing students’ autonomy and critical thinking.

items.title: Pengaruh Live Shopping, Promosi AI, dan Perceived Trust terhadap Keputusan Pembelian di E-Commerce Lazada)
items.abstract: Perkembangan e-commerce mendorong platform digital untuk menghadirkan berbagai strategi pemasaran guna meningkatkan keputusan pembelian konsumen. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Live Shopping, Promosi Berbasis Artificial Intelligence (AI), dan Perceived Trust terhadap keputusan pembelian pengguna e-commerce Lazada. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan pengumpulan data melalui kuesioner kepada pengguna Lazada. Data dianalisis menggunakan regresi linier berganda dan pengujian hipotesis secara parsial. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa Live Shopping tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian, dengan nilai signifikansi 0,223. Sebaliknya, Promosi Berbasis AI berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian dengan nilai signifikansi 0,005. Perceived Trust juga terbukti berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keputusan pembelian dengan nilai signifikansi 0,002. Hasil tersebut menunjukkan bahwa konsumen Lazada lebih terdorong oleh promosi yang relevan dan personal serta rasa percaya terhadap platform dibandingkan pengalaman berbelanja melalui siaran langsung. Penelitian ini memberikan gambaran bahwa pemanfaatan AI dan peningkatan kepercayaan konsumen dapat menjadi strategi penting dalam mendorong keputusan pembelian pada e-commerce.

items.title: Perancangan Meja Belajar Lipat Ergonomis Berorientasi Pengguna dengan Pendekatan Ergonomic Function Deployment dan Kearifan Lokal di Perguruan Tinggi
items.abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang meja belajar lipat minimalis yang ergonomis dan berorientasi pada pengguna di lingkungan perguruan tinggi, menjawab tantangan keterbatasan ruang hunian mahasiswa. Penelitian perancangan produk ini melibatkan 30 responden mahasiswa dengan karakteristik usia rata-rata 21 hingga 23 tahun, jenis kelamin pria dan wanita, tinggi badan rata-rata 160 cm, di fakultas teknik yang dipilih secara purposive sampling. Metode yang digunakan meliputi Ergonomic Function Deployment (EFD) untuk menerjemahkan kebutuhan pengguna menjadi karakteristik teknis, pengukuran antropometri untuk validasi dimensi fisik, dan Morphology Product untuk pengembangan alternatif desain yang mengintegrasikan kearifan lokal. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan penerjemahan delapan kebutuhan pengguna menjadi target teknis presisi, seperti tinggi meja 72 cm dan dimensi lipat 60 cm. Data antropometri selanjutnya memvalidasi dimensi tersebut secara objektif, memastikan kesesuaian postur dan ruang kaki yang inklusif bagi berbagai tipe tubuh. Tahap morfologi menghasilkan konfigurasi optimal berupa meja bersudut membulat, mekanisme flat folding yang aman, rangka aluminium hollow, serta sentuhan finishing natural beraksen lokal betawi. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa integrasi EFD, antropometri, dan morfologi produk sangat efektif menghasilkan furnitur edukatif yang tidak hanya memecahkan masalah efisiensi ruang dan kenyamanan postur, tetapi juga memiliki nilai kultural. Luaran penelitian ini menghasilkan rancangan teknis dan prototype konseptual (model CAD) dan analisis kelayakan manufaktur yang belum dilakukan pada tahap ini. Penelitian ini berkontribusi pada integrasi EFD, antropometri, dan morfologi produk dalam perancangan furnitur edukatif yang hemat ruang, ergonomis, dan bernilai kultural.

items.title: Performance of Artificial Intelligence in the Diagnosis of Periapical Periodontitis Based on Cone-Beam Computed Tomography: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: This systematic review assessed the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI) for detecting periapical periodontitis on cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). A systematic literature search of Scopus, PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase was conducted to identify peer-reviewed diagnostic studies involving human participants and published up to August 30, 2026. Studies evaluating the application of AI for the detection of periapical periodontitis on CBCT were deemed eligible for inclusion. Conversely, studies focusing exclusively on periapical cysts, other odontogenic lesions, or root resorption were excluded. The risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies–Artificial Intelligence (QUADAS-AI) tool, while the certainty of the evidence for the pooled outcomes was evaluated according to the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Of 659 records identified through database searches, 18 studies were included in the systematic review and 6 in the meta-analysis. The exploratory HSROC synthesis yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.91 (95% CI, 0.84-0.94) and a pooled specificity of 0.94 (95% CI, 0.80-0.98). Substantial between-study heterogeneity was observed, with I² values exceeding 98% for virtually all reported metrics, and the corresponding prediction regions were wide. Consequently, the pooled estimates should be interpreted solely as exploratory descriptive summaries rather than as clinically generalisable estimates of diagnostic performance. The GRADE certainty of evidence was rated as very low for each of the four pooled outcomes. The diagnostic performance and clinical utility of AI for the detection of periapical periodontitis on CBCT remain uncertain, owing to the extreme heterogeneity, wide prediction regions, and very low certainty of evidence identified in this review. These findings support further investigation rather than routine clinical implementation at present. AI warrants further evaluation as a potential adjunct to clinician-led assessment of periapical periodontitis. The current evidence does not establish clinical benefit or justify recommending routine use or replacement of professional judgement.

items.title: Phase change material-based thermal energy storage: a review of current trends, research evolution, and growing role of artificial intelligence
items.abstract: Abstract Thermal energy storage (TES) using phase change material (PCM) is one of the key technologies to improve energy efficiency and integrate renewable energy. This study aims to systematically map the research evolution, emerging themes, major contributors, and technological developments in PCM-based TES research from 2000 to 2025. A PRISMA-based bibliometric analysis was conducted using 5612 publications retrieved from the Scopus database and analyzed using Bibliometrix and VOSviewer. The analysis examines publication trends, leading countries and journals, collaboration networks, citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic evolution. With an above 60% share of the publications after 2018, it shows the rapid development in this field, with China and India being the main contributors. The research areas have developed from the fundamental characterization of PCMs to nano- and composite PCMs, heat transfer enhancement, battery thermal management, building energy applications, and sustainable energy systems. The application of artificial intelligence and machine learning in TES modeling, prediction, optimization, and intelligent control is shown in emerging research clusters, which demonstrates a growing trend. The findings identify key research directions and gaps, particularly in optimizing nano/composite PCM formulations, validating PCM performance under realistic operating conditions, and developing experimentally validated AI/ML models. This review offers a structured knowledge of the development of PCM-based TES research and identifies some specific opportunities for the development of efficient, reliable, and application-oriented thermal energy storage technologies.

items.title: Philosophy, Ethics and Artificial Intelligence a Human-Centred Framework for Responsible Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) has developed from a specialised area of computer science into a general-purpose technology that increasingly influences education, healthcare, finance, employment, communication, governance and everyday decision-making. This expansion makes AI not only a technological subject but also a philosophical and ethical concern. This conceptual research paper examines the relationship between philosophy, ethics and artificial intelligence from a human-centred perspective. It analyses the ethical significance of human dignity, autonomy, privacy, justice, fairness, transparency, accountability, responsibility and sustainability. The study uses qualitative conceptual analysis of philosophical literature, AI ethics scholarship and major institutional frameworks. Particular attention is given to deontological ethics, consequentialism, virtue ethics and selected Indian ethical ideas. The paper further examines algorithmic bias, surveillance, opacity, manipulation, employment transformation, education, environmental impact and the problem of assigning responsibility for AI-mediated decisions. Contemporary frameworks of UNESCO, OECD, NIST and NITI Aayog are examined as important attempts to translate ethical principles into governance and risk-management practices. The analysis indicates that responsible AI cannot be achieved by technical safeguards alone. Ethical reasoning needs to be integrated across the complete AI lifecycle, from problem formulation and data selection to design, testing, deployment, monitoring and retirement. A human-centred framework is proposed around eight principles: human dignity, human agency, non-maleficence, justice and inclusion, privacy, explainability and contestability, accountability, and sustainability. The paper concludes that the fundamental question for the AI era is not merely what machines can do, but what human purposes, values and limits should guide their development and use.

items.title: Precision Agriculture Using AI for Crop Yield Prediction and Disease Detection: A Comprehensive Review of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Approaches for Sustainable, Data-Driven Farming
items.abstract: Abstract Precision agriculture amalgamates artificial intelligence (AI) with field-level sensors to enhance agricultural yield while reducing resource use. This article offers an extensive examination of the application of machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) methodologies to two essential functions: forecasting crop production based on environmental and soil information, and identifying plant diseases using leaf images. We investigate the historical evolution of the discipline, outline prevalent data sources and preprocessing methodologies, evaluate the reported efficacy of prominent model families across various benchmark analyses, showcase representative case-study workflows, and assess the resource and economic implications of AI-assisted agriculture. We provide a deeper examination of regional deployment trends, delineate the practical and technological obstacles hindering large-scale implementation, and suggest prospective research avenues such as federated learning, edge deployment, and interpretable AI. The evaluation aims to function as a comprehensive resource for scholars and professionals exploring this swiftly advancing domain.

items.title: Predictors of Motivation for English Language Learning among University Students in Helmand Province, Afghanistan
items.abstract: Although English is taught in Afghan universities, the factors that motivate students in Helmand Province to learn it remain under-researched. This study examined how intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation, and English learning confidence shape overall motivation to learn English in Helmand Province, Afghanistan. A quantitative correlational design was used to collect data through a structured questionnaire from 324 male students across four universities (Helmand University, Bost University, Arakozia University, and Wadie Helmand University) using multi-stage stratified random sampling. Each construct was measured using five items rated on a 5-point Likert scale. The study used descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, Pearson correlation, paired-sample t-test, and multiple regression. The results indicated high overall motivational levels (M = 4.39, SD = 0.63), and intrinsic motivation (M = 4.38, SD = 0.53) was significantly higher than extrinsic motivation (M = 3.95, SD = 0.83), t = 10.03, p <. 001. The correlational analysis revealed a significant positive correlation among all variables (p < .001), and English learning confidence had the strongest correlation with overall motivation (r = .623). The multiple regression analysis indicated that the three predictors explained 45.4% of the variance in overall motivation (R2 =.454). The findings suggest that while both intrinsic and extrinsic motivations are important, students in the target universities are highly influenced by internal factors. This study emphasizes the importance of psychological factors in sustaining motivation among university students in Helmand Province.

items.title: Privacy And Data Protection Challenges in The Era of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) structures rely on large amounts of private records for training and deployment. This creates privacy concerns that common fact safety systems now would not have been designed to handle, along with opaque statistical series, net scraping without meaningful consent, inferences about sensitive features, leakage of training statistics from models, surveillance, and automated decision making. The rapid development of generative AI has heightened those concerns, as fashions that are proficient on internet-scale data currently are used by tens of millions of those who mechanically embed private records into them. It assesses the main legal frameworks, particularly the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the EU AI Act, and India’s Digital Personal Information Protection Act, 2023, and identifies gaps in how they handle inferred facts, educated fashions, and enforcement of erasure rights. It also considers regulatory enforcement enjoy, consisting of actions against Clearview AI and ChatGPT, to show how current regulation is applied to AI in practice. Finally, it evaluates technical security measures consisting of differential privacy and connected knowing, along with organizational measures consisting of privacy-by-design, impact assessments, and independent audits. The paper argues that effective security requires the implementation of legal responsibilities mixed with privacy-preserving engineering, instead of either on my own, and that responsibility should be shifted upstream to people who design, train, and deploy AI systems. It concludes with suggestions for regulators, with special reference to the Indian context.

items.title: Psychological Adaptation and Intervention Strategies for Generations Alpha and Beta: A Comparative Study on Evolving Lifestyles and Mental Health Needs
items.abstract: Generation Alpha (born 2010-2024) and Generation Beta (born 2025-2039) represent an unprecedented developmental archetype defined by total digital integration and ubiquitous artificial intelligence (AI). This empirical study evaluated specialized psychological adaptation mechanisms, parenting models, and mental health intervention frameworks across these cohorts. Utilizing a mixed-methods design, quantitative data were gathered from $N = 300$ parents (Gen Alpha parents and expectant/early Gen Beta parents) using the Modified Parental Stress Scale (PSS) and Child Behavior Checklist (CBCL), supplemented by qualitative interviews with $N = 20$ pediatric mental health experts. Independent samples $t$-tests confirmed that Gen Alpha/Beta display significantly higher digital dependency anxiety ($M = 38.60, p < .001$) alongside superior visual-spatial intelligence ($M = 44.10, p < .001$) relative to normative baselines. Crucially, a proactive "Digital Integration" co-navigation parenting framework yielded significantly lower parental stress ($M = 29.50$) compared to rigid "Digital Detox" restriction models ($M = 42.80, p < .001$). A preventive clinical framework focusing on Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) and cognitive impulse management is proposed.

items.title: Psychologically Friendly Schools: The Impact of School Well-Being on Islamic Primary School Student Engagement
items.abstract: A psychologically friendly school environment is related to school well-being and student involvement in learning. Although these two aspects have been extensively researched, empirical evidence in the context of Islamic primary schools in Indonesia still needs to be expanded. This study aims to describe school welfare and student involvement and analyze the relationship between the two in grades IV–VI. The study uses a quantitative approach with an ex post facto correlational design. A total of 57 students were selected through purposive sampling techniques. Data were collected using a Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed through descriptive statistics, normality tests, linearity tests, and simple linear regression. The results showed that school well-being and student involvement were in the moderate category. There was a positive and significant relationship between the two variables (Y = 7.756 + 0.484X; t = 4.744; p < 0.001; R = 0.539). A value of R² = 0.290 indicates that school well-being explains 29% of the variation in student engagement. items.title: Public Health and Digital Technology: Opportunities, Challenges and A District-Level Framework for Parbhani, Maharashtra
items.abstract: Abstract Digital technology has become an important component of contemporary public-health systems. Telemedicine, mobile health applications, electronic health records, digital identity, health information systems, remote monitoring, artificial intelligence and data analytics can support prevention, early detection, referral, continuity of care and population-level surveillance. India has developed a substantial digital-health ecosystem, including the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) and eSanjeevani. WHO describes digital health as an area with major potential to improve access, decision-making and health-system performance, while also emphasizing equity, interoperability and responsible implementation. [1–5] This paper examines the relationship between public health and digital technology with special reference to Parbhani district of Maharashtra. It uses a narrative review and policy-analysis approach based on WHO documents, Government of India sources, Census material and recent peer-reviewed literature. The paper discusses potential applications in primary healthcare, maternal and child health, nutrition, noncommunicable disease management, infectious-disease surveillance, health education and referral services. Particular attention is given to the rural–urban digital divide, digital literacy, connectivity, privacy, cybersecurity, interoperability and workforce readiness. A district-level framework is proposed to connect community-level workers with digital registration, teleconsultation, electronic records and public-health analytics. The paper argues that technology should complement rather than replace human-centred public-health services. For Parbhani, a phased approach combining infrastructure, training, assisted digital access, data governance and local evaluation can support more equitable digital health development.

items.abstract: With the extended SEQUAL framework presented in Chap 3 , we can examine aspects of the quality of models for man and machines more systematically. We start with an example of how to assess the quality of symbolic models for human use, building on earlier work using SEQUAL to evaluate ontologies, and extending it to include aspects of the renewed framework. Then we present a case study of a machine learning system in which the quality of the results depends on both symbolic and sub-symbolic models. In Sect. 4.3, we discuss how sustainability considerations are important when selecting ML techniques for data at various points along the pipeline. Section 4.4 ends the chapter by investigating the quality of explanation models in XAI.

items.title: Race, Embodiment, and Professionalism: A Critical Intersectional Analysis of Brazilian Sign Language Interpreting
items.abstract: This paper investigates the intersections of race, corporate professionalism, and somatic regulation within Brazilian Sign Language (Libras) translation and interpretation. While traditional translation scholarship prioritizes linguistic neutrality, this study employs an interdisciplinary critical methodology combining Critical Race Theory (CRT), Critical Discourse Analysis (CDA), and Translation and Interpreting Studies (TIS) to deconstruct how standard professional aesthetics inadvertently sustain systemic racism and Eurocentric cultural erasure. Utilizing a textual deconstruction of Article 5 of the National Libras Code of Ethics alongside an autoethnographic mapping of workplace visual ergonomics, we examine how racialized aesthetic expectations regulate and pathologize cultural markers such as braided hairstyles, Black power aesthetics, and turbans. Furthermore, we analyze technical workplace barriers through a TIS lens, including contrastive shirt mandates, stage lighting calibration, and professional turn-taking ergonomics. By interrogating these parameters, we expose the underlying institutional discourses and translational norms that pressure Black interpreters to alter their unalterable phenotypes to comply with a normalized, white somatic standard, ultimately arguing for an anti-racist reconfiguration of interpreter ethics and material practices.

items.title: Radiation Therapists as a Human Safety Barrier in Radiotherapy: Detecting, Reporting, and Learning from Near-Miss Events
items.abstract: Background: Radiotherapy is a complex process involving many professions and many handovers of information, with error opportunities at every step. Most errors are intercepted before they reach the patient, and radiation therapists (RTTs), who carry out the final verification and delivery steps, are the professional group that most often detects them. Objective: To review the evidence on how RTTs detect, report and learn from near-miss events, and to propose a framework for strengthening this human safety barrier. Methods: A narrative mini-review of peer-reviewed literature, incident learning system reports (ROSIS, SAFRON, RO-ILS), professional guidance (AAPM, ASTRO, ICRP, IAEA, WHO, UK safer-radiotherapy publications) and human-factors research. Results: Errors arise most often in planning, simulation and documentation, but therapists are the largest single group of discoverers in multi-institutional and international databases. RTTs detect errors through independent verification, image-guided review (CBCT, kV/MV, surface guidance), observation in the treatment room and communication with the team. Detection is shaped by training, workload, situation awareness and the design of technology. Reporting is limited by fear of reprimand, hierarchy, slow systems and cognitive biases that make intercepted events seem not worth reporting. Psychological safety and just-culture principles increase reporting. Learning requires analysis at the level of the system, corrective action and feedback. Automation reduces some errors but creates new failure modes and automation bias. Conclusions: RTTs are active safety barriers, not passive operators. We propose a Detect-Intercept-Report-Analyze-Learn-Improve-Reassess framework with RTT competencies defined for each stage, and we call for standard definitions, RTT-led investigation, safety competencies in RTT education, and AI that supports rather than replaces the vigilance of RTTs.

items.abstract: Annotatsiya: Mazkur maqolada zamonaviy qurilish loyihalarini boshqarishda Building Information Modeling (BIM) texnologiyasidan foydalanishning ilmiy va amaliy jihatlari tadqiq etilgan. BIM texnologiyasining 3D modellashtirishdan tashqari loyiha ma’lumotlarini boshqarish, qurilish jarayonlarini muvofiqlashtirish, vaqt va xarajatlarni nazorat qilish hamda obyektning ekspluatatsiya bosqichidagi ma’lumotlarni boshqarish imkoniyatlari tahlil qilingan. BIM texnologiyasining Common Data Environment (CDE), openBIM, IFC, 4D va 5D modellashtirish, Internet of Things (IoT), sun’iy intellekt va Digital Twin texnologiyalari bilan integratsiyasi ko‘rib chiqilgan. Tadqiqot natijasida BIM asosida qurilish loyihalarini boshqarishning integratsiyalashgan modeli taklif etilgan. Shuningdek, O‘zbekiston qurilish sohasida BIM texnologiyalarini joriy etishning mavjud holati va rivojlanish istiqbollari tahlil qilinib, BIM mutaxassislarini tayyorlash, elektron hujjat aylanishi va raqamli axborot muhitini rivojlantirish bo‘yicha takliflar ishlab chiqilgan. Kalit so‘zlar: BIM, raqamli qurilish, raqamli transformatsiya, 3D modellashtirish, 4D BIM, 5D BIM, CDE, openBIM, IFC, Digital Twin, IoT, sun’iy intellekt, qurilish boshqaruvi. Abstract: This article examines the scientific and practical aspects of using Building Information Modeling (BIM) technology for managing modern construction projects. The study analyzes BIM not only as a three-dimensional modeling technology but also as an integrated information management approach for coordinating project participants, controlling construction time and costs, and managing information throughout the life cycle of a building. The integration of BIM with Common Data Environment (CDE), openBIM, IFC, 4D and 5D modeling, Internet of Things (IoT), artificial intelligence, and Digital Twin technologies is considered. Based on the analysis, an integrated BIM-based construction project management model is proposed. The current development and implementation of BIM technologies in the construction sector of Uzbekistan are also discussed. Particular attention is paid to BIM education, electronic document management, information exchange, and the development of digital construction management infrastructure. The proposed approach can contribute to improving project coordination, reducing information inconsistencies, increasing resource efficiency, and supporting data-driven decision-making throughout the construction life cycle. items.title: Recent advances in deep eutectic solvent pretreatment for the efficient decomposition and utilization of crop straw biomass
items.abstract: The comprehensive and high-value utilization of crop straw biomass (CSB) is pivotal to advancing sustainable agricultural development and achieving the dual-carbon goals, owing to its low-carbon nature, renewability, and abundance. However, the efficient exploitation of CSB is severely hindered by its structural recalcitrance and heterogeneity, making an effective pretreatment technology to overcome this bottleneck. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have been considered as the most promising green solvents for CSB pretreatment, which not only possess excellent properties but also exhibit prominent advantages including low toxicity, low preparation cost, good biodegradability and recyclability. This review elaborates on the latest research progress of the DESs (especially novel supramolecular DESs) in CSB pretreatment. It further summarizes cutting‑edge DES‑coupled pretreatment technologies, machine‑learning‑assisted DES optimization, techno‑economic analysis and life‑cycle assessment for DES‑based biorefinery. Mitigation strategies and future research directions are proposed, including polyol‑assisted suppression of lignin condensation, machine‑learning‑driven DES screening, and multi‑dimensional mechanistic exploration via advanced characterization and theoretical simulations. Moreover, the review summarizes the diverse high-value application pathways of DES-pretreated CSB in the generation of platform chemicals, biofuels and materials. The challenges faced in the scaling-up of DES-based pretreatment technology to industrial applications are analyzed. Frontier research opportunities are also highlighted, encompassing the development of advanced analytical tools, integrated characterization of interactions between lignin and carbohydrates, and artificial intelligence‑driven innovation within biorefinery systems. The review provides a theoretical basis and practical guidance for the development of lignocellulosic biorefinery approaches, and is of great significance for alleviating the global energy crisis and addressing major environmental issues.

items.title: Relevansi Nilai-Nilai Peradaban Islam dalam Pengembangan Pendidikan Modern di Era Digital
items.abstract: Islamic civilization is one of the major civilizations that has significantly contributed to the development of science and education worldwide. During its golden age, it established educational institutions, fostered scholarly traditions, and produced influential scholars whose ideas continue to shape modern knowledge in the digital era. This article examines the relevance of Islamic civilizational values to the development of modern education through qualitative library research using thematic content analysis. The findings show that Islamic education was distinguished by four interrelated values, namely a strong culture of literacy, the integration of religious and general knowledge, an emphasis on moral formation (akhlak), and openness to knowledge from other civilizations, which together enabled scholars to advance science while upholding ethical and social responsibility. These values are highly relevant to addressing contemporary educational challenges, including declining critical literacy, uncritical dependence on digital technology and artificial intelligence, and the ongoing crisis of learners’ character. These values can inform the development of a modern educational system that integrates critical thinking, digital literacy, character education, and lifelong learning while maintaining moral and social responsibility.

items.title: Responsible Management of Artificial Intelligence in Education: Balancing Innovation, Ethics, and Student Well-Being
items.abstract: Abstract Integration of AI in the educational system is rapidly changing the face of education by offering new possibilities of personalized learning and efficient management at the same time creating serious issues related to student autonomy, data security, and psychology. The paper suggests a holistic framework for the management of AI in education by using recommendations for the responsible use of AI in various spheres developed by international organizations like UNESCO together with recent findings about the psychological state of students. We suggest that successful integration of AI into educational practices should be based on a transition from technology-based management of AI to human-based one where student well-being becomes one of the major ethical considerations.

The documentary discrepancy requires dated protocol/SAP amendments and monitoring records; it does not establish outcome-driven stopping or invalid treatment results. items.title: Rethinking Rural Extension: Towards More Flexible Agricultural Innovation Systems from a Sociotechnical Perspective
items.abstract: Although agricultural extension methodologies have been widely studied, limited attention has been paid to the mismatch between field technicians’ methodological preferences and institutional constraints from a socio-technical systems perspective. This study analyzes rural extension methodologies in Latin America during 2022–2025, focusing on interactions among local and scientific knowledge, social actors, and territorial innovations. A qualitative, descriptive-documentary approach was adopted, incorporating comparative content analysis of 20 selected scientific publications and international reports on rural innovation systems. Evidence was extracted using structured multidimensional analytical matrices covering pedagogical, operational, and structural dimensions, then examined through comparative thematic analysis and theoretical triangulation. The reviewed evidence indicated a reported preference of 34.6% for individual extension methods, including farm visits, associated with their capacity to build mutual trust and support situated learning. It also identified a reported institutional mismatch of 28.4%, linked to rigid, top-down administrative regulations that constrain methodological choices. These findings challenge the assumption that individual extension is inherently hierarchical and highlight its pedagogical potential within agricultural innovation systems. The study contributes to agricultural innovation systems theory and the literature on socio-technical transitions by emphasizing the relationship between extension practices and institutional conditions. It concludes that methodological flexibility and socio-pedagogical competencies are important for extension agents and supports the design of adaptable, context-sensitive public advisory policies that accommodate diverse extension approaches.

items.title: Revolutionary transformation of digital art:ontological reconstruction and paradigm shift driven by technology
items.abstract: Abstract This study examines changes in digital art’s creative mechanisms, subject relations, and conditions of existence through the lens of the philosophy of technology. Tracing the evolution from mechanical and electronic media to algorithmic systems, the paper argues that technology no longer functions merely as an external tool but increasingly intervenes in artistic cognition, creative processes, and the conditions under which works are generated. The paper outlines three notable dimensions of change in digital art: technologically mediated existence, distributed creative relations, and algorithmically shaped aesthetic processes. The paper also examines three tensions: Western aesthetic dominance via biased training data, NFT-driven value paradoxes, and destabilized artistic subjectivity under generative AI. Drawing on process philosophy, complexity theory, and technological phenomenology, it proposes a techno-cognitive framework positioning digital art as a dynamic interface between technology and human cognition. The study proposes evaluative and ethical discussion frameworks better suited to contemporary digital art, with the aim of supporting further theoretical analysis.

items.title: Robust NLP for Social Good: Transformer-Based Classification of Noisy Disaster-Related Social Media Messages
items.abstract: Abstract In the wake of terrible occurrences, social media has become the preferred source for real-time information. Social media has become a significant instrument for victims of catastrophes to express their needs, document incidents, request support and share information related to their situation. However, automated analysis may be fairly difficult in the case of casual, abbreviated, grammatically inconsistent, spelling-variant and other textual noisy communications. Artificial intelligence may be used to this data to enhance the response to catastrophes provided by technology and the well-being of humans and help in the improved detection and organization of communications related to disasters. The current research is a study on the feasibility of the use of Natural Language Processing (NLP) based on transformers to classify the social media postings about the tragedy with background noise. A social media dataset related to catastrophes is pre-processed adequately to develop classification models. For the comparison of the performance of the handling of textual content on catastrophes a transformer-based model and a conventional machine-learning baseline are taken into consideration. Some of the main performance indicators used to evaluate the models include accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score. The problems caused by casual and distracting social media text are given specific attention. This project aims to (1) describe the challenges of collecting and evaluating noisy user-generated data and (2) empirically evaluate transformer-based text categorisation in a disaster-response setting. The research explores the use of AI-driven natural language processing on social media platforms connected to catastrophes to assist in the timely comprehension of crisis-related communication and human well-being. Moreover, it adds to the greater issue of Artificial Intelligence for social benefit.

items.abstract: The operating theatre is a complex high risk clinical environment that can create challenges to patient safety. Miscommunication, incorrect surgery/procedure on the wrong patient, medication errors, equipment issues, retained surgical items, physiological decline and delayed detection of complications can all cause issues to patient safety. Artificial intelligence is becoming an important tool within the operating theatre to improve patient safety by analysing large volumes of data.

items.title: Safety and Usability of a Novel, Robotic Assistance System for Echocardiographic Examination
items.abstract: Background: Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) is essential for modern cardiac diagnostics, yet it is difficult to access in remote areas. Remotely operated robotic-assisted ultrasound may enable access to services in rural and remote locations, while also improving ergonomics for the sonographer. This study evaluated the safety, usability and patient satisfaction of a novel robotic ultrasound assistance tool (RUAT). Methods: This open-label, single-site, single-arm clinical trial enrolled adult participants who had recently completed a standard manual echocardiogram. A trained sonographer performed a robot-assisted TTE from a dedicated workstation in the same room as the patient. Endpoints included safety measured by adverse events, technical and clinical usability, and patient satisfaction using surveys about the participants’ experience. Results: The trial cohort (n=30; mean age 62.9 ± 17.5 years; 70% men) all successfully completed the robot-assisted TTE and the patient satisfaction survey. There were no adverse events or adverse device effects. The functional verification checklist supporting technical usability demonstrated an average usability rate of 96.9% (95% CI [98.9–100.0]), with a 100% rate across 10 of 12 metrics. The sonographer’s review of the acquired robotic images measured the clinical usability and 29 of 30 examinations met acceptable diagnostic standards (96.7%; 95% CI [88.1–100.0]). The mean participant satisfaction score was 8.3 out of 10, with 96.7% scoring ≥6. Conclusion: The RUAT demonstrated high technical and clinical usability, as well as high acceptance by participants. These findings indicate that robot-assisted TTE is a viable strategy to enhance remote access to TTE services.

items.title: Salivary Multi-Omics Biomarkers Using Artificial Intelligence for Early Oral Cancer Detection and Risk Classification
items.abstract: Background: Oral cancer continues to be a significant health issue worldwide, and a late diagnosis is highly correlated with poorer treatment outcomes and shorter life expectancy. While these two steps (examining a patient and obtaining tissue cultures) are essential to this diagnosis (previously routine), they do not help to detect the patient in time at the population level. A minimally invasive, biological fluid such as saliva has many molecular components that may mirror pathological changes occurring in the oral cavity. Salivary omics domains could thereby yield a better assessment, through a combination of the domains, of the risk of oral cancer at an early stage. Artificial intelligence (AI) may further enhance the analysis of complex molecular patterns by integrating information from multiple salivary biomarker domains. Such approaches may support the identification of potential early indicators of oral cancer and improve the classification of individuals according to their estimated disease risk. Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the potential of multi-omics salivary biomarkers (genomic/transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and microbiome) for the early detection and risk classification of oral cancer. The study also highlights the potential application of AI-based analytical approaches to integrate multi-omics biomarker information and clinical characteristics for improved oral cancer risk classification. Methods: The approach applied was quantitative cross-sectional and analytical, and involved a number of respondents of 279 people. Demographic and behavioural risk factors and the perception of being assessed for these risk factors by biomarkers were investigated, along with oral symptoms, clinical findings, and salivary multi-omics classifications. Normality test and Cronbach's Alpha reliability test, Bartlett's Test of Sphericity, and KMO Test, Independent Samples t test, One-Way Analysis of Variance, Kruskal-Wallis, Chi-Square Test of Independence, Pearson correlation and regression analysis were used in statistical analysis. Results: The results showed a good level of reliability with an average Cronbach's Alpha of 0.901 - 0.938. Supporting construct validity is the value of kmo which is excellent (0.959), and the Bartlett's test result shows that the p-value is less than 0.001. Gender difference, differences in age groups, differences in category of areca use and cooked chew (areca/users, non-users), differences in Betel chewing (areca, non-users) were the significant differences. The overall multi-omics risk classification was well correlated with the clinical examination status, χ² (9) = 429.967, p < 0.001. Overall multi-omics risk revealed significant associations between domains of major biomarkers, with the highest between clinical examination and overall multi-omics risk. The regression analysis resulted in a highly significant predictive model of overall risk classification (R = 0.943, R² = 0.889, p < 0.001), which explained a great variance of risk predictors that were included in the model. Conclusion: Results showed that the multi-omics biomarkers of saliva were a prevalent candidate for use as a minimally invasive tool to aid early detection/classification of OCD. Combination of use of molecular biomarker domains with clinical examination may lead to improved identification of patients likely to show symptoms of a clinical disorder that would warrant early diagnosis referral. The disease diagnosis performance needs to be further tested in other populations before the wide-scale application of the system. Future studies should investigate the integration of salivary multi-omics biomarkers using appropriately validated AI models, with particular attention to early cancer detection, risk classification, model interpretability, and external validation across independent populations.

items.title: Serum Creatinine Levels among Motorcycle Workshop Mechanics in Carbon Monoxide-Prone Workplaces: A Photometric Study
items.abstract: Motorcycle workshop mechanics work in environments where vehicle exhaust may accumulate, particularly in workshops located near dense traffic and with limited ventilation. Carbon monoxide (CO) is not directly measured in this study; therefore, daily working hours and years of employment are used as occupational indicators of possible long-term exposure. This descriptive cross-sectional study analyzed serum creatinine levels among 30 motorcycle workshop mechanics on Jalan Riau, Pekanbaru. Respondents were selected by purposive sampling based on predefined eligibility criteria. Venous blood was collected, processed into serum, and analyzed using an Optiva photometer with a Glory Diagnostics enzymatic creatinine kit at 510 nm. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize creatinine distribution by age, daily working duration, and length of employment. The results showed that 17 respondents (56.67%) had serum creatinine levels above the reference range (>1.3 mg/dL), while 13 respondents (43.33%) had normal levels (0.7-1.3 mg/dL). Increased creatinine levels were more frequent among mechanics working 12 hours/day (75%) than among those working 8 hours/day (20%), and were also more common in respondents aged 30 years or older and those with more than 10 years of employment. These findings suggest that mechanics with longer occupational contact in CO-prone workshop environments may have a higher proportion of elevated serum creatinine. However, because ambient CO or carboxyhemoglobin was not measured, the results should be interpreted as an occupational-health screening finding rather than evidence of direct causality. Improved ventilation, routine health monitoring, and occupational safety education are recommended.

items.title: Seven Names, One Life: A Lexicon Biography of Satish Gajawada (IIT Roorkee Alumnus)
items.abstract: Biographies usually follow a life forward in time, and independent researchers who work outside institutions are rarely documented in a structured way. This article addresses the lack of critically labelled biographical accounts of independent artificial intelligence researchers by studying Satish Gajawada, a 2012 graduate of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee whose fourteen years of independent work are distinguished by the coining of names for research fields, algorithms, a society, a title and a family of “theories of everything”. The purpose is to read this life through its vocabulary and to separate what has been named from what has been validated. The study uses a lexicon method: five source documents supplied by the subject were analysed, and seven terms were treated as biographical entries, each examined as an event, a method and a question for assessment. Every factual statement was labelled as documented, self-reported or interpretive. The principal results show a recurring “self and others” grammar that links philosophy to optimisation; an expanding programme of proposed fields; a large catalogue of themed swarm algorithms without reported comparative evaluation; a 2026 turn toward family-based ethics; and a growing practice of disclosure, including a small reproducible fairness test in which a penalty term reduced a demographic-parity gap from about 0.12 to 0.016 at a cost of about 1.9 percentage points of accuracy. The article concludes that the most defensible contribution is a consistent human-centred vocabulary for artificial intelligence, that adoption and independent validation remain unreported, and that the subject’s growing candour about the limits of his claims is the most significant recent development. Keywords: research ethics; artificial intelligence; biography; particle swarm optimisation; independent research; value-aligned artificial intelligence

items.abstract: Rapid urbanization, increasing motorization, and spatial concentration ofemployment and services are putting increasing pressure on urban road networks. Trafficcongestion is not only a transportation problem, but also a multidimensional urbanplanning problem that affects travel time, economic productivity, energy consumption,air quality, road safety, and social amenity. This paper explores the relationship betweenroad infrastructure and traffic congestion, identifies the main mechanisms that causerecurrent and non-recurrent congestion, and systematizes engineering, planning, policy,and digital interventions. A literature-based analytical approach is used, combiningclassical theories of demand, network balance, and bottleneck effects with recentevidence on demand management policies, intelligent transportation systems (ITS),artificial intelligence, and integrated urban mobility. The analysis shows that increasingroad capacity alone cannot guarantee sustainable reductions in congestion, as additionalcapacity may encourage additional car traffic. Road network improvements are morelikely to achieve sustainable results when combined with adaptive traffic signalmanagement, public transport prioritization, parking and demand management,coordinated land-use planning, real-time information, and multimodal accessibility. Aconceptual framework is proposed that considers road capacity, traffic demand, networktopology, control quality, and passenger behavior as interacting variables. The paperconcludes with recommendations for developing cities, which are particularly relevantfor the rapidly developing urban centers of Central Asia.

items.title: Sit Posture Classification using XGBoost Algorithm Based on Wearable Sensor Data
items.abstract: Prolonged non-ergonomic sitting posture during computer-based learning activities poses a risk of musculoskeletal disorders, yet current posture monitoring systems are largely static and neglect temporal aspects. This study develops a real-time posture classification system integrating accelerometer-based wearables with the XGBoost algorithm, specifically designed for university students. Data were collected from 21 subjects using two MPU6050 sensors placed on the thoracic and lumbar areas, yielding 28,054 data rows. Preprocessing involved mean imputation for missing values, removal of non-feature columns, and exclusion of gyroscope data due to extreme outliers. Feature extraction using 30-sample non-overlapping windows generated 24 statistical features (minimum, maximum, mean, standard deviation) from the accelerometer axes. As the primary benchmark for generalization, the XGBoost model was evaluated using Leave-One-Person-Out Cross-Validation (LOPOCV), achieving an average accuracy of 73.76% with balanced precision and recall scores (0.73–0.75), indicating consistent performance when encountering new subjects. Feature importance analysis identified az2_max (score: 0.1087) and az1_mean (score: 0.1053) as the most dominant features. Meanwhile, as an initial feasibility test under controlled conditions, real-time testing with five subjects (50 instances) reached 100% accuracy, with a web monitoring interface successfully displaying posture status, confidence values (53–81%), and posture-change logs, alongside a buzzer mechanism that activated appropriately upon detecting non-ergonomic postures. This system demonstrates the potential of low-cost accelerometer-based wearables for effective real-time posture monitoring; however, its performance is significantly influenced by individual physical characteristics such as height and weight. Consequently, future research is advised to diversify the dataset and implement personalization techniques to enhance generalization across broader populations.

items.abstract: Skin cancer is most common diseases find in humans worldwide and early detection can be assist to improve the doctors’ diagnosis. Traditional diagnosis depends on visual examination by dermatologists using dermoscopy also time consuming and depends heavily on the experience of the clinician or doctor. In recent years, deep learning has become the leading approach for automatic detection and classification skin lesions from dermoscopic and clinical images. In this paper we present a focused review of the most recent deep learning methods, published recently, for skin cancer detection and classification. The review covers benchmark datasets, image preprocessing and classification and segmentation methods, and major deep learning architectures, which include convolutional neural networks (CNNs), hybrid CNN-Transformer models, vision transformers, generative adversarial networks (GANs), and multimodal fusion approaches. It also summarizes the main challenges that still limit the real-world use of these systems, such as complex lesion features, image noise, intra-class variation, inter-class similarity, and class imbalance. In this paper we discuss future research directions, such as explainable artificial intelligence, fairness across different skin tones, and uncertainty-aware models. Keywords— Skin cancer; deep learning; dermoscopy; convolutional neural network; vision transformer; image classification; class imbalance

items.abstract: A smart city is defined as a city that employs communication and information technologies to enhance the entire process of governance, including making it more effective, public access to data, and enhancing the quality of government services alongside the well-being of citizens. Rapid population growth creates problems for cities associated with urban transport, air pollution, energy inefficiency, water scarcity, waste disposal issues, and burden on urban infrastructure. Smart city solutions include using new technologies, such as the Internet of Things (IoT), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Cloud Computing, Big Data Analytics, Geographic Information System (GIS), 5G, and intelligent sensors, for efficient resource management. Smart city technologies help monitor different aspects in real time and make intelligent decisions in the areas of transport, health, energy supply, waste management, and public safety. In India, the Smart Cities Mission has made cities implement several technology-based initiatives for sustainable development and citizen engagement. In this research paper, the concept, design, technologies, applications, advantages, problems and perspectives of smart cities are examined, taking into account their applications in India.

items.abstract: ABSTRACT. As urban areas transform into intelligent ecosystems, artificial intelligence technologies are assuming an increasingly vital role in the prevention of urban crime. This research amalgamates artificial intelligence with conventional criminological theories, specifically Routine Activity Theory (RAT) and Crime Pattern Theory (CPT) to theorize framework and practical approaches to urban crime prevention. To methodically evaluate the convergence of artificial intelligence implementation in urban crime deterrence. AI implements predictive policing and real-time monitoring, establishing a novel kind of oversight that perpetually observes metropolitan environments, hence diminishing prospects for criminal activity. This study contends that multidisciplinary methodologies for urban crime prevention, integrating technology with social and spatial theories, yield more successful and nuanced solutions. The findings convey a definitive message: although technology and urban design are significant, the primary emphasis for effective crime prevention is in education, preventive measures, and the strategic integration of digital tools.

items.abstract: Abstract The global community stands at a critical crossroads where technological advancement and environmental preservation must converge to ensure human well-being. This paper explores the multidisciplinary approach required to navigate global futures, focusing on the harmonization of economic science, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and digital innovation with sustainability metrics. Focusing specifically on the drought-prone Sangola Taluka of Solapur District, Maharashtra, this study examines how traditional agrarian economies can transition into sustainable models using precision farming. With over 73.96% of the workforce in Solapur engaged in agriculture, yet suffering from an average rainfall of less than 545-750 mm, integrating AI-driven resource frameworks is crucial. The paper provides factual insights into the pomegranate economy of Sangola and highlights how digital interventions can optimize water use, mitigate economic risks, and align local systems with Environmental Sustainability. Critical interventions such as IoT sensors, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for pathological tracking, and decentralized drone application systems are detailed to model an optimal input-to-output agricultural grid.

items.title: Smart Farming Using Applications of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: Abstract Agriculture is one of the key sectors in the global economy and is a key component of food security, rural employment and sustainable development. But, there are certain serious problems in the modern agriculture like climate change, scarcity of water, degradation of soil, rise in production cost, labour scarcity, crop diseases, attack by pests, and food demands. The collection of periodic observations and experience of traditional farming methods may not always be sufficient and reliable information for making complex decision making in agriculture. Smart farming, with the assistance of Artificial Intelligence (AI), can be a data-driven solution to solve these challenges. With AI, one can gather and process vast amounts of data from sensors, satellites, drones, weather stations, farming equipment, and mobile devices, and then take action on that information. The use of machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, robotics, Internet of Things (IoT), predictive analytics and decision-support systems is gaining traction in agriculture. These technologies can help farmers in the selection of crops, soil testing, precision irrigation, fertilizer management, pest/disease detection, yield prediction, weed management, harvesting, livestock monitoring, and supply-chain management. This research paper reviews the significant applications of Artificial Intelligence in smart farming, its benefits, technical architecture, challenges and future prospects. The study was conducted based on the analysis of recent studies published in the literature on 6R (AI, Precision Agriculture, AIoT, Smart Irrigation, Remote Sensing, and Machine Learning). Recent systematic reviews suggest crop monitoring, irrigation, pest and disease management, yield prediction, nutrient management, robotics, and protected cultivation are key areas where AI is applicable. The paper concludes that with the proper infrastructure, farmer training, reliable data, and affordable technologies, AI can play a significant role in productive, efficient, climate-resilient, and sustainable agriculture.

items.title: SmartLab: AI-Based College Laboratory Equipment Tracking and Predictive Maintenance System
items.abstract: College laboratories contain equipment that must be identified, tracked, and maintained to support practical learning. Manual registers and periodic inspections can make it difficult to know the current status of each item, find maintenance history quickly, and identify equipment that may need servicing. SmartLab proposes a software-based system for registering laboratory equipment, tracking its status, maintaining service records, and using equipment usage and maintenance history to estimate maintenance needs. The application provides a staff dashboard for equipment registration, tracking, maintenance updates, and reports. Equipment can be assigned a unique ID and a status such as Available, In Use, Faulty, or Under Maintenance. A predictive-maintenance module can analyse recorded usage and service history to flag equipment for inspection. The system is intended to improve record accessibility, support timely maintenance, and reduce avoidable disruption in college laboratories. Predictions are decision-support suggestions and should be verified by laboratory staff. items.title: Social and Pedagogical Drivers of ChatGPT Acceptance: An Extended TAM Model in Teacher Education
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence tools, particularly applications such as ChatGPT, hold significant potential to reshape the landscape of teacher education by offering opportunities for personalized feedback and adaptive learning. These tools also play important roles in teachers’ pedagogical decisions while designing their teachings in present learning environments. However, the underlying mechanisms driving pre-service teachers’ adoption of such particular tools remain under-explored. This study addresses this gap by validating an extended technology acceptance model incorporating constructivist teaching beliefs, subjective norms, facilitating conditions, ChatGPT self-efficacy, and perceived enjoyment. Data collected from 488 senior pre-service teachers in Türkiye were analyzed using structural equation modeling. Results show that ChatGPT self-efficacy and perceived enjoyment significantly predict perceived ease of use, whereas facilitating conditions do not exert a significant influence. Perceived usefulness is significantly associated with perceived ease of use, subjective norms, and pedagogical beliefs. Behavioral intention is significantly associated with perceived usefulness, subjective norms, and ChatGPT self-efficacy, with the framework explaining 54% of the variance. Given the cross-sectional nature of the data, these results offer tentative implications for teacher education. Practically, the findings highlight the potential value of scaffolded micro-teaching and institutional verification procedures for supporting responsible and equitable generative AI use in teacher education. Further recommendations are discussed in the light of teacher education procedures and policies.

items.abstract: Abstract This retrospective study compares standard knowledge distillation (KD) and decoupled knowledge distillation (DKD) fo​r lightweight artificial intelligence-based​ radiographic knee osteoarthritis grading. GhostNetV2 students learned five Kellgren–Lawrence grades from a Swin-Tiny teacher and were evaluated against a cross-entropy baseline using an Osteoarthritis Initiative-derived dataset of 8260 images from 4130 patients with patient-disjoint partitions. Across three​ runs, mean binary triage accuracy was 84.04%, 84.82%, and 84.82% for baseline, standard KD, and DKD. Thresholds targeting at least 90% validation specificity yielded test sensitivities of 72.77%, 76.56%, and 75.50%, with specificities of 92.09%, 90.94%, and 91.12%; these operating points are not specificity-matched. Mean five-class accuracy was 64.63%, 67.63%, and 67.71%. Separate illustrative checkpoints showed reduced KL-1-to-KL-2 overcalls with DKD (28.0 to 18.9%) but lower KL-0 recall (90.6 to 78.7%). Calibration, exploratory decision curves, and patient-cluster uncertainty intervals were evaluated. Each student contains 4.88 million parameters. Distillation improved mean performance internally, but decoupling did not demonstrate an additional sensitivity benefit over standard KD. No external cohort or clinician-supported decision policy was evaluated; clinical utility and population-level stability remain unestablished.
